fields.value: Autonomous computer-vision pipeline: robots detect and track faces, recognize identities, estimate face pose and gaze direction, compute face-to-robot scores, and send these to a central server. Local and centralized Hungarian algorithms perform identity matching and global robot-human allocation; robots then provide audio, visual, and movement feedback.

quotes.text: Each robot detects faces in the video stream from its camera, and the identity of each detected face is recognized using a pre-trained face identity classifier using the ROS face recognition package.
All robots send their face scores for each human identity to a central server, which uses the Hungarian algorithm to determine which robot is most likely being looked at by which human.
The face score is calculated using Equation 4.
Once a robot is notified that a human is gazing it, the robot performs sound, visual and movement feedback.

fields.value: The paper presents an autonomous vision system in which three people select among three mobile robots by looking at them. Face identity and gaze estimates are shared across robots to allocate selections, including when a selected robot cannot see the person; reported scenario success ranged from 60% to 100%.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5; RQ6 — It describes gaze-based selection and its role in assigning robots to people, reports technical selection performance and camera-related limitations, and details the sensing, allocation system, and robot platform. It does not assess effects on participants’ subjective experience.
